# Ting 0.7.4
## New
- Micro-apps can now ask for text during a run with an `ask` step. It supports an initial `default`, a `placeholder`, optional input with `required: false`, and a multiline editor with `multiline: true`. Return continues in a single-line field; Command-Return continues in a multiline editor. - A `choose` step shows a filterable list from the previous step. Supply one option per nonempty line or a JSON array of strings or objects with `title`, optional `subtitle` and string `value`. Up/Down selects and Return confirms. Only the selected value reaches the next step; even one option requires confirmation. An empty list stops the run. - Both steps pass their answer to the next step and expose it as `${steps.ID}` when an `id` is set. Esc cancels the entire run. Answers are not remembered, and waiting does not consume execution timeouts, including inside libraries. They require Ting's panel: `ting-micro check` validates the file, but headless `ting-micro run` rejects interactive steps before running any part of it. - Settings now lets you choose the macOS system sound played when the leader menu opens and set its volume. Choosing a sound or releasing the volume slider previews it. The config keys are `sound` (default `Tink`) and `soundVolume` (0 to 1, default 0.5); an unavailable name falls back to `Tink`.
## Fix
- A copy of Ting installed with Homebrew no longer runs Sparkle. It does not check for updates on its own and never shows the Sparkle update window. - In such a copy, Ting's menu (the menu-bar icon and the gear of selecta and launcha) and the Updates section of Settings offer **Update Ting via Homebrew…** instead of **Check for Updates…**. It runs exactly `brew upgrade --cask --greedy bobuk-io/tap/ting` with the `brew` of the Homebrew prefix that installed Ting. It never upgrades anything else. - A window shows the command, the live output of brew and the real result: updated, already up to date, cancelled, or the error with brew's output and exit code (for example no network, a Homebrew lock or a password prompt that cannot be answered). If Ting stops while brew replaces it, a copy of Ting made before brew started shows the progress window until the end, even while no Ting.app is installed. After an update, Ting starts again from its installed place and shows the same result. A copy that you downloaded yourself still updates with Sparkle, as before. - The launcher (selecta or launcha) now stays on the screen, in the same state, when the gear opens Ting's menu. Before, it closed first. While the menu is shown, the launcher and the leader and launcha hotkeys do not react to keys. If the menu closes with no choice, the launcher takes keys again.
## Cause
Before this release, Ting started Sparkle in every release copy that had an update feed and key. It never checked who installed the app, so a copy that Homebrew manages offered Sparkle updates too. Ting now counts a copy as Homebrew-managed only when a Caskroom record `<prefix>/Caskroom/ting/<version>/Ting.app` of the cask `ting` resolves to the running Ting.app. Ting looks in `/opt/homebrew`, `/usr/local`, `HOMEBREW_PREFIX` and the prefix of a `brew` found in `PATH`. In an unclear case Ting keeps Sparkle.
The exact error of the Sparkle install in a Homebrew copy was not reproduced for this release, so its cause is not known. This release no longer runs Sparkle in such a copy, so that failure cannot occur there.
## Upgrade
A downloaded copy: choose **Check for Updates…** in Ting. A Homebrew copy of 0.7.3 or older still has the Sparkle update; quit Ting, run `brew upgrade --cask --greedy bobuk-io/tap/ting` in a terminal, and open it again. Later updates then work from Ting's menu. Settings, bindings, micro-apps and permissions are preserved. Requires macOS 14 or later; the signed, notarized and stapled universal app supports Apple Silicon and Intel.
